clips.label: Question 1
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Two-Part Scope of Work Structure. When reviewing a new integration contract before mobilizing to the site, a lead CTS-I installer separates the scope of work into deliverable scope and project scope. What is the key distinction between these two scope components? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Deliverable scope defines the features and functions of the product or service provided, whereas project scope defines the work activities required to accomplish delivery. Option B. Deliverable scope lists only owner-furnished hardware, whereas project scope lists only contractor-furnished hardware. Option C. Deliverable scope covers post-closeout preventive maintenance, whereas project scope covers initial needs analysis. Option D. Deliverable scope is restricted to architectural drawings, whereas project scope is restricted to audio DSP programming.

clips.label: Question 2
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Work Breakdown Structure Noun Convention. While reviewing project management charts during pre-installation planning, how are elements formatted in a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) compared to a Logic Network Diagram? Choose the single best answer. Option A. WBS elements are stated as verbs with calendar dates, whereas Logic Network elements are stated as cost codes. Option B. WBS elements are stated as nouns representing deliverables, whereas Logic Network activities are stated as verbs connected by dependencies. Option C. Both WBS and Logic Network elements list assigned technician names and hourly billing rates. Option D. WBS elements show room elevation views, whereas Logic Network elements show conduit fill percentages.

clips.label: Question 2, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. WBS elements are stated as verbs with calendar dates, whereas Logic Network elements are stated as cost codes. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "WBS elements are stated as verbs with…stated as cost codes" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) decomposes project deliverables into nouns without specifying who, when, or how much, whereas a Logic Network Diagram sequences activities written as verbs according to predecessor and successor dependencies. Best answer: WBS elements are stated as nouns representing deliverables, whereas Logic Network activities are stated as verbs connected by dependencies.

clips.label: Question 3
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Effort versus Duration Scheduling. Why does estimating an installation schedule using 'effort' rather than 'duration' frequently cause schedule overruns on an AV project? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Effort automatically doubles the required technician headcount for every task. Option B. Duration ignores weekends, holidays, and multi-project resource contention. Option C. Effort measures only pure best-case labor hours for a task without accounting for travel, delays, holidays, or competing project demands. Option D. Effort can only be calculated after substantial completion has been signed.

Spray water over the open equipment racks to settle the airborne dust.

clips.label: Question 26
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Single Distribution Board Power Readiness. When verifying AC mains power readiness for an AV system spanning a control room and an adjacent auditorium rack, why should all AV branch circuits originate from a single electrical distribution board and phase? Choose the single best answer. Option A. To allow the AV installer to bypass circuit breakers during live events. Option B. To minimize differences in earth/ground potential between interconnected racks that cause 50/60 Hz ground-loop hum. Option C. To double the AC mains frequency from 60 Hz to 120 Hz. Option D. To eliminate the need for equipment grounding conductors on the racks.

clips.text: Work from the governing relationship or dependency, not from memory alone. clips.label: Question 36, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Vertically on end in the freight elevator so the roller tube bears the weight. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Vertically on end in the freight elevator…tube bears the weight" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: Roller projection screens must always be stored and transported horizontally (carrying them vertically causes the fabric to telescope and wrinkle on the tube) and carried with the slot facing down so the bottom batten bar does not jam. Best answer: Horizontally with the screen case slot facing down.

segments.text: When setting up cable reels in the staging area prior to a pull, how must bulk cable be dispensed from the spool to prevent kinks and conductor geometry distortion?

segments.label: Response instruction
segments.text: Choose the single best answer.

segments.label: Option A
segments.text: Option A. Mount the spool on a wheeled or stationary cable caddy/drum holder so the spool rotates freely and dispense cable from the bottom of the reel.

segments.label: Option B
segments.text: Option B. Lay the spool flat on its side on the floor and pull loops off the top flange.

segments.label: Option C
segments.text: Option C. Unwind the entire 300 m spool into a random pile before starting the pull.

segments.label: Option D
segments.text: Option D. Use a forklift to stretch the cable taut across the parking lot.

clips.label: Question 51, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Mount the spool on a wheeled or stationary cable caddy/drum holder so the spool rotates freely and dispense cable from the bottom of the reel. Correct. Correct: Laying a spool flat on its side twists the cable every turn and causes kinks; spools must spin freely on a cable caddy with cable pulled smoothly from the bottom of the drum. CTS-I cue: identify the signal type, path, interference control, routing function, and published cable limits before choosing or testing the link.

clips.label: Question 52
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Daily Progress Report Contents and Purpose. Why must a lead CTS-I installer submit regular Progress Reports (PRs)—often accompanied by dated site photographs—into the project management and construction management systems? Choose the single best answer. Option A. To replace the need for final as-built drawings at project closeout. Option B. To document work completed as of a specific date and flag any site, schedule, or trade issues that could impact the project timeline or budget. Option C. To allow technicians to change the contracted scope of work without informing the client. Option D. To calculate the acoustic critical distance of the auditorium.

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Letter of Transmittal Function. Choose the single best answer. Option A. An unsigned verbal memo. Option B. A blank purchase order. Option C. clips.label: Question 55
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Documenting Control Button Discrepancies During Testing. During onsite control testing with the client present, pressing a touch-panel button triggers a different behavior than the client expected. How should the CTS-I document and communicate this event? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Calmly record only what the button actually did in the field test report and escalate to the PM/programmer—never say 'It's broken' or promise free programming changes. Option B. Tell the client the programmer made a mistake and promise to rewrite the macro for free. Option C. Refuse to write anything down so there is no paper trail of the test. Option D. Give the client the programmer's laptop password so they can edit the script themselves.

clips.label: Question 72
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Post-Tension Concrete Slab Coordination with GC. Before drilling anchor holes into a concrete ceiling in a high-rise office building, the installer learns the floor slabs are post-tensioned concrete. What coordination step is mandatory before any drilling occurs? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Switch to a larger masonry bit and drill twice as deep. Option B. Consult the general contractor/structural engineer and have specialists locate or X-ray the embedded high-tension steel cables before drilling. Option C. Use water to cool the drill bit while cutting through the steel tension tendons. Option D. Shoot powder-actuated fasteners randomly across the slab.

clips.label: Question 73
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Ceiling Grid Coordination for Tile Bridges. When installing recessed loudspeakers in a suspended acoustic tile ceiling, how must the loudspeaker weight be supported to avoid sagging tiles or code violations? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Rest the loudspeaker magnet directly on the acoustic mineral-fiber tile. Option B. Tie the loudspeaker to the nearest fire-sprinkler branch pipe with nylon zip-ties. Option C. Use a load-rated tile bridge that transfers weight to the ceiling grid rails and anchor a secondary seismic/safety support wire to the building structure per AHJ code. Option D. Glue the speaker bezel to the bottom of the tile with silicone caulk.

Cancel the projector installation and leave the mount on the floor.

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Signed Change Order Prerequisite Before Scope Addition. While the crew is pulling cables in a training room, the client's department head walks in and asks the lead installer to add two extra wall displays and HDMI wall plates. How must the installer respond? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Install the extra displays immediately using spare truck stock and bill the client verbally. Option B. Remove two loudspeakers from the room to keep the total project cost unchanged. Option C. Politely explain that any addition to scope requires routing the request through the Project Manager for a formal signed Change Order (CO) before work can proceed. Option D. Refuse to speak to the client and walk off the job site.

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Correcting VPN MTU Packet Fragmentation on Video Streams. During commissioning of a multi-site corporate videoconferencing link over an encrypted VPN tunnel, video streams stutter severely even though only 30% of the link bandwidth is in use. Protocol analysis reveals fragmented packets exceeding 1518 bytes. What configuration modification fixes the issue? Choose the best destination for the match. Option A. Replace all Cat 6A patch cords with unshielded Cat 3 telephone wire. Option B. Change the room cameras from progressive scan to interlaced scan. Option C. Reduce the video endpoint's maximum frame/MTU size so that adding the VPN encryption header does not push frames past the 1518-byte Ethernet MTU limit. Option D. Assign the video codec a link-local 169.254.x.x APIPA address.

clips.label: Question 85, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Replace all Cat 6A patch cords with unshielded Cat 3 telephone wire. Incorrect. Not this one: "Replace all Cat 6A patch cords with unshielded Cat 3 telephone wire" names a related term or action, but its function does not match the specific definition or decision requested here. Decisive rule: VPN encryption encapsulates packets in an extra header; if the resulting frame exceeds the 1518-byte Ethernet MTU limit, routers fragment each packet into two frames, ruining real-time media timing. Switch the measurement microphone from omnidirectional to figure-8.

clips.label: Question 90
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Ceiling Projector Substructure and Pipe Rigging Sequence. Arrange the steps for installing an overhead ceiling-mounted projector substructure and suspension pipe in the correct chronological sequence. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Verify structural engineer approval, confirm the 5:1 safety factor for combined device and hardware weight, and hand-check ceiling beams for HVAC vibration. Step 2: Anchor the adjustable steel-channel strut (Unistrut) bridge to primary building structure and attach the upper pipe flange. Step 3: Drop a plumb bob from the pipe flange to mark the ceiling tile, remove the tile to hole-saw the opening cleanly, and reinstall the tile. clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Prohibition on Drilling Steel I-Beams / RSJs. What is the mandatory rule when attaching an AV substructure or steel-channel strut to a structural steel I-beam (Rolled Steel Joist / Universal Beam)? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Never drill into a structural steel I-beam; use rated beam clamps (or approved welding by a certified welder) to attach steel-channel strut.

clips.label: Question 100
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Concrete Expansion Anchor Hole Cleaning Requirement. After drilling a hole into a solid concrete slab with a rotary hammer drill to install a mechanical or chemical expansion anchor, what step is critical before inserting the anchor? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Fill the hole with cable pulling lubricant so the anchor slides in easily. Option B. Enlarge the mouth of the hole by wobbling the spinning drill bit in circles. Option C. Drive a wooden dowel into the hole alongside the steel anchor. Option D. Blow or vacuum all pulverized concrete dust out of the hole so the anchor grips solid masonry rather than loose powder.

clips.label: Question 104
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Staggered Cable Snout Construction Rules. When building a staggered cable snout to pull a multi-cable bundle through a raceway, which cable is placed in the lead position and how far apart are the remaining cables staggered? Choose the single best answer. Option A. The thinnest optical fiber is placed in front, with all other cables taped flush at the exact same tip. Option B. The shortest coax cable is placed in front, with 1 meter gaps between cables. Option C. A bare copper ground wire is tied in a square knot at the tip without tape. Option D. The longest and strongest (largest gauge) cable is placed in the lead, with each subsequent cable staggered 75–100 mm (3–4 in.) behind and secured with a slip knot 600 mm (2 ft) back, half-hitches, and smooth flexible tape.

clips.label: Question 104, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. The thinnest optical fiber is placed in front, with all other cables taped flush at the exact same tip. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "The thinnest optical fiber is placed in…at the exact same tip" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: A proper cable snout places the longest, heaviest-gauge cable in the lead, staggers remaining cables in 75–100 mm (3–4 in.) steps, anchors the pull string with a slip knot 600 mm (2 ft) from the tip plus 3–4 half-hitches, and wraps stretched tape into a smooth, flexible cone. Best answer: The longest and strongest (largest gauge) cable is placed in the lead, with each subsequent cable staggered 75–100 mm (3–4 in.) behind and secured with a slip knot 600 mm (2 ft) back, half-hitches, and smooth flexible tape.

clips.label: Question 105
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: No Cable Left Behind 4-Step Cable Pulling and Labeling Workflow. Order the four steps of the 'No Cable Left Behind' temporary cable labeling and pulling workflow in the exact sequence performed in the field. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Apply a matching temporary ID label ~600 mm (2 ft) from the leading end of the cable AND onto the supply spool. Step 2: Pull the cable along the designated pathway to its destination without exceeding tension or bend-radius limits. Step 3: Transfer the ID label from the supply spool to the trailing end of the cable (~600 mm / 2 ft from the cut point). Step 4: Cut the cable free from the supply spool.

clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Crossing AC Power and Signal Cables at 90 Degrees. Connect the audio shield to the neutral busbar of the lighting dimmer pack.

clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Solid versus Stranded Conductors for Infrastructure Pulling. clips.label: Question 118
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Hybrid versus Composite Optical Fiber Cable Construction. When pulling specialized fiber trunk cables for broadcast cameras or campus racks, what distinguishes a 'Hybrid' fiber cable from a 'Composite' fiber cable? Choose one labeled answer area. Option A. A Hybrid cable combines optical fibers and copper power conductors under one jacket (e.g., for HD cameras), whereas a Composite cable combines both single-mode and multimode optical fibers under one jacket. Option B. A Hybrid cable uses plastic fiber, whereas a Composite cable uses hollow air tubes. Option C. A Hybrid cable is for underwater use only, whereas a Composite cable is for aerial poles only. Option D. There is no difference; both terms describe standard Cat 5e UTP.

clips.label: Question 120
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Drilling Finished Wood Surfaces Without Exit Splintering. When drilling a through-hole in a finished wood lectern or architectural panel during rough-in, how should the installer drill to prevent ugly splintering on the visible side? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Use a concrete masonry hammer drill at maximum speed from the back side. Option B. Punch the hole through with a claw hammer. Option C. Drill from the finished side toward the unfinished back side (or, if finished on both sides, drill a small starter pilot hole through and enlarge from both sides). Option D. Heat the drill bit red-hot with a blowtorch to burn through the wood.

According to AVIXA F502.02:2020 (Rack Design for Audiovisual Systems), when assembling a freestanding or mobile equipment rack that is NOT bolted to the building structure, how must the equipment weight be distributed? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Place all heavy UPS battery packs and analog power amplifiers in the top 6 RUs. Option B. Distribute weight evenly from top to bottom with the heaviest unit at eye level. Option C. Place at least 50% (half) of the total equipment weight in the bottom third of the rack to maintain a low center of gravity and prevent tipping. Option D. Hang the heaviest amplifiers from the rear cable lacing bars only.

clips.label: Question 128
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Evacuation versus Pressurization Rack Cooling Methods. Why does a 'pressurization' active rack cooling system—which blows filtered cool air into the bottom of the rack—keep internal electronics cleaner than an 'evacuation' top-exhaust fan system? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Pressurization cools the rack using liquid nitrogen. Option B. Evacuation fans spin backward and push room dust down the chimney. Option C. Pressurization creates positive internal air pressure through an intake filter, pushing air outward through cracks and vents so unfiltered room dust cannot be sucked into the rack. Option D. Pressurization seals the rack hermetically with zero airflow.

clips.label: Question 129
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Rack Assembly and Population Sequence per AVIXA F502.01. Place the shop rack-population and assembly steps in the safest, standards-compliant sequence per AVIXA F502.01. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Lay the rack horizontally on its back over a padded blanket on the shop floor and verify rail squareness. Step 2: Install the heaviest equipment (UPS units and power amplifiers) in the bottom third of the rack, supporting deep chassis on rear rails. Step 3: Mount user-operated media/control gear at ergonomic eye/reach height, high-heat gear near the top, and RF receivers with front-mounted antennas, starting all rack screws by hand. Step 4: Install blanking/vent panels in all unused RU spaces to control airflow and bond the rack chassis and doors to the single technical ground stud.

clips.label: Question 133
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Isolating Rack Technical Ground from Building Conduit Steel. How should an AV equipment rack be grounded and connected to incoming metallic building conduits so that noisy building structural currents do not corrupt the AV technical ground? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Weld the top of the rack directly to the building's steel I-beam and elevator shaft. Option B. Remove all ground wires from the rack so it floats above earth potential. Option C. Maintain a single dedicated path to technical ground via the rack's grounding stud/scraped bare-metal busbar, and isolate the rack from metal building conduits using plastic conduit couplings/troughs at rack entry. Option D. Rely solely on the painted rack-ear screws of a plug-in power strip to ground the cabinet.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: IEC Class II Double-Insulated Equipment Symbol and Grounding Rule. What does this IEC symbol indicate, and how should the chassis be grounded? Choose the single best answer. Option A. It indicates a 3-phase 480 V industrial motor that requires three ground straps. Option B. It indicates a PoE+ network switch that must be bonded to a cold water pipe. Option C. It indicates a rack shelf that requires cage nuts. Option D. It identifies IEC Class II (double-insulated) equipment, whose chassis must NOT be connected to earth ground.

clips.label: Question 137, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Bundles must be twisted together into a single central braid. Incorrect. Not this one: "Bundles must be twisted together into a single central braid" names a related term or action, but its function does not match the specific definition or decision requested here. Decisive rule: Because AC mains and mic-level signals differ in voltage by ~50,000:1 (~94 dB), high-level/power bundles (Loudspeaker, RF, Power, Ground) and low-level/signal bundles (Mic, Line, Video, Control, Network) go on opposite sides of the rack with at least 100 mm (4 in.) between bundles. Best answer: At least 100 mm (4 in.) between parallel cable bundles, with low-level/signal bundles routed down the opposite vertical side of the rack.

Wall-wart power supplies must be mounted outside the building.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Swing-Frame and Slide-Out Rack Service Loop Clearances. When wiring a wall-mounted swing-frame rack or a millwork slide-out rotating rack, what critical physical check must the installer perform before closing the rack? Choose the single best answer. Swing or slide the rack through its full range of motion to verify that the umbilical service loop neither pinches/chafes on hinges nor bends tighter than the cables' minimum bend radius. Option D. Remove the rear mounting rails so the cables hang on the connectors.

clips.label: Question 143
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Unbalanced Audio Maximum Cable Length Rule. When distributing consumer line-level audio (`-10 dBV` / `316 mV` on RCA or 3.5 mm connectors) from a lectern media player to a rack mixer, what is the maximum permissible cable length for an unbalanced audio circuit, and how should longer runs be handled? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Up to 100 m (328 ft) over standard dual RCA zip cord. Option B. Up to 500 m (1,640 ft) if the shield is cut at both ends. Option C. Up to 50 m (165 ft) using speaker wire. Option D. Never exceed 5 m (16 ft) (and ideally keep under ~1 m / 3 ft); for longer runs, place a Direct Box (DI) or balancing transformer right at the source to convert the line to balanced mic/line level.

clips.label: Question 146
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Loudspeaker Impedance Meter Verification Sequence. Arrange the steps for verifying a distributed loudspeaker circuit with an AC impedance meter (`Z`-meter) in the correct order. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Disconnect the loudspeaker circuit completely from the power amplifier output terminals and calculate the expected total impedance (ZT). Step 2: Select the appropriate ohm range on the AC impedance meter and calibrate the meter to that scale. Step 3: Connect the impedance meter leads to the disconnected speaker line and read the measured AC impedance. Step 4: Verify the reading is within ±10% of the calculated impedance (troubleshooting any low-Z shorts or high-Z opens) before connecting the line to the amplifier.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Digital Video Cliff Effect and Passive HDMI Barrel Couplers. Why does joining two 5 m (16 ft) passive HDMI copper cables with a passive barrel coupler frequently result in a completely blank screen ('cliff effect') when switching from 1080i to 4K60 UHD? Choose the single best answer. Option A. 4K60 UHD uses lower frequencies than 1080i. Option B. Option C. Passive couplers strip out the green color channel only. Option D. HDMI cables only carry analog RGBHV signals.

segments.text: Which five signal categories ('5Play') can an IEEE 1911 HDBaseT transmitter/receiver pair transport simultaneously over a single Category 5e/6+ cable up to 100 m (328 ft)?

segments.label: Response instruction

segments.label: Option A

To check if the manufacturer hid the warranty card inside the screw hole. Option D. Step 3: Drill and anchor the first end of the screen case at the calculated height. Step 4: Level the screen case horizontally with a spirit level, anchor the second end, and test smooth extension and retraction.

The center of the actual projection viewing surface (not the center of the outer metal housing), while leaving service access to the motor end. Option C. The right-hand end cap of the metal case. Option D. The wall light switch beside the door.

Second-surface bathroom mirrors should be glued directly to drywall.

clips.label: Question 161
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Wireless Diversity Antenna Spacing and Metal Clearance. When mounting pair of remote UHF diversity antennas for a wireless microphone receiver system, what minimum spacing between the two antennas and clearance from metal surfaces must be maintained? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Tape both antennas together side-by-side onto a steel air duct. Option B. Space the diversity antennas at least 100 m apart using 75-ohm RG59 video coax. Option C. Space the two diversity antennas at least 1 m (3 ft) apart (and > 1/4 wavelength) and keep them at least 300 mm (1 ft) away from metal surfaces, using 50-ohm low-loss coaxial cable. Option D. Submerge the antennas in the ceiling sprinkler pipe.

clips.label: Question 162
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Coaxial BNC Cable Stripping and Linear Compression Termination Sequence. Place the steps for terminating a 75-ohm coaxial video cable with a linear-compression BNC connector in the proper sequence. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Slide any required boot/label sleeve onto the cable and calibrate a 3-blade rotary coaxial stripping cassette for the exact cable and BNC model. Step 2: Rotate the 3-blade stripper around the cable end to cut the outer jacket, braided shield, and dielectric to exact stepped lengths without nicking the center conductor. Step 3: Fold back the braided shield as specified and push the prepared cable fully into the linear-compression BNC connector until the center pin seats properly. Step 4: Squeeze the connector axially with the calibrated linear compression hand tool, apply the permanent AVIXA F501.01 label 25–300 mm from the connector, and verify continuity.

Choose the single best answer. Option A. Lead-free solder melts at room temperature without a soldering iron. Option B. Lead-free solder melts at 100°C lower than leaded solder. Option C. Lead-free solder can only be applied underwater. Option D. Lead-free solder has a melting point approximately 30°C (60°F) higher than leaded solder, requiring a higher-temperature iron and care not to melt connector insulation.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Optical Fiber Termination Safety (Black Mat and Laser Eye Safety). Which two safety practices are mandatory whenever stripping, cleaving, terminating, or inspecting optical fiber cables? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Work over a black surface mat to spot microscopic glass splinters for safe disposal, and NEVER look into a fiber end with a microscope or magnifying glass until an optical power meter confirms the fiber is dark. Option B. Sweep glass fiber shards onto the carpet and look directly into the laser transmitter with a 20× jeweler's loupe. Option C. Strip glass cladding with your teeth and test continuity with a 9 V battery. Option D. Use a red work mat and blow glass splinters into the air with compressed air.

clips.label: Question 170
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Ruggedized Field Fiber Connectors (Expanded Beam and opticalCON). For dusty outdoor live events or broadcast stadium deployments where standard exposed ceramic ferrules (LC/SC/ST) would quickly become contaminated, which fiber connector types provide dust protection? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Unshielded RJ-11 telephone plugs. Option B. Expanded-beam connectors (which use lenses to widen the beam across an air gap) and locking shuttered opticalCON connectors (housing duo/quad LC ferrules). Option C. Bare cleaved glass fibers taped together with electrical tape. Option D. 2-blade Type F coaxial twist-on connectors.

clips.label: Question 178
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: EDID Handshake Sequence Between Source and Sink. Order the phases of the digital video EDID handshake between a video Source and a video Sink (display) in chronological sequence. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: The Source sends a +5V Hot Plug signal to the Sink, and the Sink returns the Hot Plug Detect (HPD) signal confirming it is powered and connected. Step 2: The Source requests the Sink's EDID capabilities over the Display Data Channel (DDC). Step 3: The Sink transmits its EDID table (and extension blocks for audio/lip-sync) back to the Source over the DDC. Step 4: The Source configures its output and transmits the video/audio stream matching the Sink's preferred native resolution, refresh rate, and color space.

clips.label: Question 183
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: System Optimization Audio Gain Calibration Sequence (400 Hz + Piezo). Arrange the steps for setting electronic audio gain structure using the System Optimization method (`400 Hz` sine wave + piezo tweeter) in the proper order. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Turn power amplifiers OFF, neutralize all EQs/dynamics, inject a 400 Hz sine wave at 0 dBu into a mixer input, and connect a piezo tweeter (2–20 kHz) to the mixer output. Step 2: Raise the mixer master output until the piezo tweeter buzzes (clipping harmonics), then back off slightly until the piezo goes silent. Step 3: Move the piezo tweeter sequentially to each downstream processor's output up to the amplifier input, driving each stage to the onset of piezo buzz and backing off until silent. Step 4: Return to the mixer and reduce the mixer master output back down to its normal 0 (unity) operating position before calibrating mic trims and power amplifier input attenuators.

clips.label: Question 190
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Infrared (IR) Control Limitations and Three Field Tricks. An installer is attaching a wired IR emitter to the front bezel of a consumer display that has no RS-232 port. Which three field techniques help locate the hidden IR receiver window, prevent room light interference, and verify the emitter is firing? Choose one labeled answer area. Option A. Sandpaper the bezel, spray black paint over the emitter LED, and test with an SPL meter. Option B. Remove the display's glass screen, wire the IR port to 70V speaker lines, and check with a spirit level. Option C. Shine a flashlight at the bezel to spot the foggy/fuzzy IR window, place an opaque pinhole mask over the emitter to block ambient light, and view the emitter through a mobile phone/digital camera to see the flashing IR pulses. Option D. Use a magnet to locate the IR sensor, cover it with aluminum foil, and test with an impedance meter.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Inductive Reactance (XL) and Magnetic Crosstalk. Unlike capacitive reactance, how does Inductive Reactance (`XL`) change as frequency increases (`f ↑`), and how does magnetic induction affect adjacent unshielded cables? Choose the single best answer. Option A. XL drops to zero at high frequencies. Option B. XL only exists in optical glass fibers. Option C. XL increases as frequency increases (`f ↑ ⇒ XL ↑`), and alternating magnetic fields around current-carrying conductors induce unwanted voltage (hum or crosstalk) into adjacent parallel conductors. Option D. XL eliminates the need for twisted-pair cabling.

segments.label: Response instruction
segments.text: Choose one labeled answer area.

segments.label: Option A

segments.label: Option C

clips.label: Question 203, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. 28.0 Ω. Incorrect. Not this one: "28.0 Ω" uses the wrong value, unit, or relationship for the stated quantities. Decisive rule: Using ZT = 1 ÷ (1/Z1 + 1/Z2 + 1/Z3): 1 ÷ (0.25 + 0.125 + 0.0625) = 1 ÷ 0.4375 = 2.29 Ω. Notice that parallel impedance is always smaller than the lowest individual speaker impedance (4 Ω). Best answer: 2.29 Ω (`1 ÷ [1/4 + 1/8 + 1/16] = 1 ÷ 0.4375 = 2.29 Ω`).

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Series-Parallel Loudspeaker Impedance Calculation (Two Branches of Three 8-Ohm Speakers). Six 8-ohm loudspeakers are wired in a series-parallel array consisting of two parallel branches, where each branch contains three 8-ohm loudspeakers wired in series. What is the total load impedance (`ZT`) presented to the amplifier? Choose the single best answer. Option A. 48 Ω. Option B. 1.33 Ω. clips.label: Question 205
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Interpreting High versus Low Impedance Meter Readings on Speaker Lines. When testing a disconnected 70V loudspeaker line with an AC impedance meter (`Z`-meter), why is a reading much LOWER than calculated far more dangerous to the amplifier than a reading much HIGHER than calculated? Choose the best destination for the match. Option A. A low impedance reading means all speakers are unplugged and safe. Option B. A high impedance reading will instantly melt the amplifier's output transistors. Option C. Impedance meters only measure optical fiber loss. Option D. A reading much lower than expected indicates a short circuit, a backward-wired step-down transformer, or an direct 8-ohm speaker on a 70V line—which will draw excessive current and destroy the amplifier output stage.

clips.label: Question 205, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. A low impedance reading means all speakers are unplugged and safe. Incorrect. Not this one: "A low impedance reading means all speakers are unplugged and safe" names a related term or action, but its function does not match the specific definition or decision requested here. Decisive rule: By Ohm's law (I = V/Z), a much lower impedance than expected draws dangerously high current that overloads and burns out the amplifier, whereas a higher reading indicates an open branch or under-tapped transformer. Best answer: A reading much lower than expected indicates a short circuit, a backward-wired step-down transformer, or an direct 8-ohm speaker on a 70V line—which will draw excessive current and destroy the amplifier output stage.

Why does the projector display a blank or green screen when protected content is played? Choose the single best answer. Option A. 3G-SDI only carries analog audio. Option B. Option C. 75-ohm BNC connectors block progressive scan frames. Option D. The coax cable needs +48V phantom power.

clips.label: Question 210
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: ISCR Contrast Ratio Calculation and Conformance Grading. At Viewer Location 3 in a university lecture hall (Basic Decision-Making category, minimum 15:1), the average luminance of the 8 white checkerboard squares is 240 nits (`cd/m²`) and the average of the 8 black squares is 12 nits. What is the contrast ratio at Location 3, and when is a system graded 'Partially Conforms'? Choose one labeled answer area. Option A. Contrast ratio is 20:1 (240 ÷ 12 = 20:1, which conforms); a system 'Partially Conforms' if 1 to 4 locations fall below the minimum ratio by no more than 10%. Option B. Contrast ratio is 2,880:1; a system partially conforms if all 5 locations fail by 50%. Option C. Contrast ratio is 12:1; a system conforms if at least 1 location exceeds 7:1. Option D. Contrast ratio is 228:1 (240 − 12).

clips.label: Question 211
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Audio/Video Lip-Sync Blip-and-Flash Tolerance Window. When verifying audio/video lip-sync alignment using a 1-frame 'blip-and-flash' test generator (`AVP-103`), what is the standard broadcast/verification sync tolerance window, and which signal usually needs delay added? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Audio may lead video by +500 ms; add video frame delay to slow the projector down. Option B. Audio must stay within +15 ms (lead) to −45 ms (lag) for broadcast/verification (+40 ms to −60 ms general max); because video scalers/displays take longer to process frames, DSP delay is added to the audio path. Option C. Audio must lag behind video by at least 200 ms. Option D. Lip-sync only needs to be checked at the rack headphone jack, never at the seating area or streaming/recording feeds.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: SPL Meter Class 1 versus Class 2 Tolerances and A/C/Z Weighting. Under IEC 61672-1 / ANSI S1.4, what are the accuracy tolerances of Class 1 and Class 2 SPL meters, and when should A-weighting (`dBA`), C-weighting (`dBC`), and Z-weighting (`dBZ`) be selected? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Class 1 is ±5 dB and Class 2 is ±10 dB; A-weighting is for concerts and C-weighting is for quiet HVAC. Option B. Class 1 and Class 2 both have ±0.01 dB tolerance; Z-weighting rolls off everything below 1 kHz. Option C. Class 1 is ±0.7 dB (precision) and Class 2 is ±1.0 dB (general field); use A-weighting for low levels/ambient noise/speech (20–55 dB), C-weighting for high levels (85–140 dB), and Z-weighting for flat 10 Hz–20 kHz response. Option D. SPL meters measure electrical voltage in dBu rather than acoustic pressure.

clips.label: Question 218
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Unity Gain (1 kHz + DMM) versus System Optimization (400 Hz + Piezo). Why does the Unity Gain method use a `1 kHz` sine wave and a True RMS Multimeter (targeting `0.775 V` [`0 dBu`] or `1.23 V` [`+4 dBu`] at each stage), whereas System Optimization uses a `400 Hz` sine wave and a piezo tweeter? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Unity Gain sets identical input/output voltage across all stages for standard rooms (~60 dB S/N), whereas System Optimization uses a 400 Hz tone below the piezo's 2–20 kHz passband so the piezo stays silent until clipping harmonics (> 2 kHz) make it buzz—maximizing S/N and relative headroom for critical halls. Option B. A 1 kHz tone destroys piezo tweeters, whereas a 400 Hz tone cannot be read by a multimeter. Option C. Unity Gain is used only on 70V speaker lines, whereas System Optimization is used only on optical fiber. Option D. Both methods require the power amplifiers to be turned full up during step 1.

clips.label: Question 219

clips.label: Question 220
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Power Amplifier Input Attenuator Calibration and Hiss Prevention. What is the true function of the front-panel rotary knobs on a power amplifier, and what symptom occurs if an installer leaves them wide open ('all the way up') while turning the upstream DSP/mixer outputs way down? Choose the single best answer. Option A. They adjust the amplifier's AC mains power consumption; turning them up saves electricity. Option B. They adjust the loudspeaker's physical impedance from 4 ohms to 70 volts. Option C. They are input attenuators (not wattage controls) that must be set LAST by raising them from minimum just until target room SPL is reached; leaving them wide open amplifies upstream noise floors and causes constant audible system hiss. Option D. They control the room's reverberation time (RT60).

clips.label: Question 222
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: RTA Measurement Microphone Placement (Critical Distance Dc + 3 dB). Because a single-channel Real-Time Analyzer (RTA) is 'time-blind' and cannot distinguish direct loudspeaker sound from room reflections, how do you locate the proper measurement microphone position? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Inject pink noise 20 dB above ambient, walk the omnidirectional mic away from the speaker until SPL stops dropping (Critical Distance Dc), then move closer toward the speaker until SPL rises by +3 dB (staying ≥ 1 m / 3 ft from the cabinet). Option B. Press the measurement microphone directly against the tweeter grille at 0 mm. Option C. Place the microphone inside the hallway outside the room with the door closed. Option D. Hang a figure-8 ribbon microphone 10 cm below the HVAC supply diffuser.

clips.label: Question 223
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: RTA Cut-Only Equalization Rule and 6 dB Maximum Cut Limit. When equalizing a loudspeaker system with an RTA, why should the installer use the 'cut-only' method and never exceed `6 dB` of attenuation on any filter band? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Boosting EQ bands reduces amplifier power consumption. Option B. Boosting peaks eats up amplifier headroom and increases distortion, while any response dip or peak requiring more than 6 dB of correction (or showing no change on the RTA) is an acoustic phase/comb cancellation that cannot be fixed with EQ. Option C. Equalizers are physically incapable of cutting more than 2 dB. Option D. Cutting more than 6 dB reverses the polarity of the subwoofer.

clips.label: Question 227
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Camera Lighting Defects (White Holes, AGC Sparkles, and Backlight Compensation). During camera setup, a presenter standing in front of an uncovered exterior window looks dark, and enabling the camera's 'Backlight' or 'AGC' setting causes blown-out 'white holes' or grainy 'sparkles.' What is the proper permanent remedy? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Set the electronic shutter speed to 1/10,000 second to create stroboscopic motion. Option B. Control the room lighting instead of relying on electronic camera compensation: close window shades/apply ND film to reduce background contrast and add high-CRI front illumination on the presenter. Option C. Turn chroma saturation to 100% and defocus the lens. Option D. Mount the camera upside down without flipping the image.

clips.label: Question 228
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Display Calibration Sequence Using PLUGE and SMPTE/ARIB Color Bars. When calibrating a display or projector's picture controls, which adjustments must be completed FIRST using a monochrome PLUGE / grayscale pattern before adjusting Chroma and Hue with color bars? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Adjust Hue first using a solid blue screen, then set Keystone. Option B. Set Sharpness to 100% before turning the display on. Option C. Calibrate Contrast (white level) using the Super White (Step 255) bar until just below white clipping, and Brightness (black level) using Normal Black (Step 16) vs. Super Black (Step 0) PLUGE bars until barely indistinguishable—before adjusting Chroma/Hue. Option D. Adjust audio delay first to fix black level.

Zoom lenses cannot focus anywhere outside the exact midpoint.

clips.label: Question 235
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Microphone Polar Pattern Placement Relative to Loudspeakers. When aiming a cardioid or hypercardioid lectern microphone in a room with overhead loudspeakers, where are the microphone's maximum rejection nulls located to maximize gain before feedback? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Directly on-axis (0 degrees) at the front of the capsule. Option B. Cardioid has maximum rejection directly at the rear (180°), whereas hypercardioid and supercardioid have tighter side pickup with small rear lobes—so maximum rejection nulls sit off-axis toward the rear cones (~110°–125°). Option C. Omnidirectional microphones have a 40 dB null at 90 degrees. Option D. Bidirectional (figure-8) microphones reject sound equally from the front and back.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Assistive Listening System (ALS) Induction Loop and T-Coil Verification (`AP-113`). When installing and verifying an Audio Induction Loop Assistive Listening System (`AP-113`), how is the audio signal transmitted to the listener, and what must be verified across the seating area? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Via line-of-sight infrared LEDs that are blocked by sunglasses. Option B. Via 60 GHz millimeter-wave Wi-Fi. Option C. Via unbalanced RCA cables plugged into each chair. Option D. A perimeter copper loop wire driven by a current amplifier generates a magnetic field that couples directly into a hearing aid's telecoil (T-coil); verify uniform magnetic field strength, frequency response, and low EMI hum across the seating area.

clips.label: Question 244
clips.text: Exam area E. Topic: Projection Screen Surface Cleaning Direction (Bottom to Top). If a front-projection screen surface gets dusty or smudged prior to closeout handover, how should it be cleaned according to Chapter 10 of the CTS-I Exam Guide? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Spray lacquer thinner across the top and let it drip downward. Option B. Scrub horizontally with a stiff wire brush. Option C. Blot edges with a clean soft brush and gently wipe from bottom to top with mild water and a clean absorbent sponge (so dirty water never streaks down over dry fabric). Option D. Remove the fabric and run it through a commercial washing machine.

Email the 400-page C++ control compiler manual to the company CEO without meeting anyone. Option D. Conduct training in the noisy loading dock before the equipment is installed.

clips.label: Question 256
clips.text: Exam area E. Topic: Handling Out-of-Scope Feature Requests Raised During Training. Halfway through an end-user training session, an attendee asks why the 'Presentation' button doesn't also brew coffee and lower the hallway shades, and asks you to reprogram it right now. What is the correct response? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Open the control code on your laptop and spend 4 hours rewriting the system for free. Option B. Tell the attendees that the system designer was incompetent. Option C. Explain that the system was programmed to the approved contract specification, note their request, and direct any desired feature additions to the Project Manager for a formal Change Order. Option D. Unplug the touch panel and end the training session immediately.

clips.label: Question 264
clips.text: Exam area E. Topic: Organizing Equipment Manuals in the Closeout Package (`DOC-117`). According to Chapter 16 of the CTS-I Exam Guide, what is the best practice for organizing manufacturer equipment manuals in the closeout documentation binder (and where should a copy of operational documentation be kept)? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Staple all manuals together in random order and mail them to the equipment manufacturer. Option B. Shred all manuals unless the client pays an extra storage fee. Option C. Arrange manuals in alphabetical order AND grouped by function (e.g., all audio manuals together, all display manuals together), and leave a copy of the operational documentation right with the AV equipment rack. Option D. Sort manuals by the weight of the paper and lock them in an off-site bank vault with no copy at the rack.

clips.label: Question 272
clips.text: Exam area E. Topic: Documenting Final Amplifier Attenuator and EQ Settings Against Tampering. After completing audio gain structure and room equalization, why should the technician record (or photograph) all physical amplifier attenuator positions and install security covers over front-panel knobs before closeout? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Security covers increase the amplifier's output wattage by 3 dB. Option B. Photographing knobs automatically updates the DSP firmware. Option C. To document the verified baseline calibration in the closeout record and prevent unauthorized users from turning knobs and ruining gain structure or blowing speakers. Option D. To block cooling air from entering the front of the amplifier.

segments.text: At project closeout, why must the finalized Network Device Inventory—including as-installed MAC addresses, IP assignments, VLANs, open TCP/UDP ports,firmware versions, and administrative credentials—be formally handed over to the client's IT department?

segments.label: Response instruction
segments.text: Choose one labeled answer area.

segments.label: Option A
segments.text: Option A. So the IT department can block all AV traffic permanently.

segments.label: Option B
segments.text: Option B. Because MAC addresses are required to calculate room reverberation time.

segments.label: Option C
segments.text: Option C. So IT can publish the admin passwords on the public company website.

segments.label: Option D
segments.text: Option D. To support ongoing enterprise network monitoring, security auditing (RP-C303.01), firmware lifecycle management, and rapid hardware replacement.

Best answer: To support ongoing enterprise network monitoring, security auditing (RP-C303.01), firmware lifecycle management, and rapid hardware replacement.

Adjust the multimeter calibration screws randomly until it reads 100 V on a 9 V battery.

clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Maintaining Sharp Cutting/Stripping Tools and Safety Tagging Power Tools. Why must dull utility-knife blades, wire strippers, and drill bits be sharpened or replaced immediately, and what periodic compliance check applies to mains-powered hand tools on job sites? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Dull blades cut faster through Kevlar fiber. Option B. Dull blades require excessive force and skip/jump dangerously (causing lacerations), while mains-powered tools require intact guards, ground pins, and periodic electrical safety testing and tagging (PAT tags). Option C. Safety guards on circular saws should be wired open during maintenance. Option D. Mains-powered drills should have their ground pins clipped off.

clips.label: Question 288
clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Maintaining Ceiling Projector Alignment Without Digital Keystone Shortcuts. During a semi-annual maintenance check, a ceiling-mounted projector's image has drifted slightly off the screen border. What is the proper maintenance procedure? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Apply 15 degrees of electronic keystone correction from the handheld remote and leave. Option B. Move the projection screen 300 mm to the right without telling the client. Option C. Inspect the structural mount, pipe threads, and setscrews for looseness or vibration, mechanically realign and lock the mount, verify optical focus/geometry, and record the work in the Maintenance Log. Option D. Zoom the lens smaller so a 500 mm black gap surrounds the image.

clips.label: Question 290
clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Number-One Cause of Electronic System Failures (Faulty Connections). According to the troubleshooting principles in Chapters 11 and 17 of the CTS-I Exam Guide, what is the single most common cause of hardware faults in audiovisual systems, and what is the Golden Rule when testing changes? Choose the single best answer. Option A. The majority of problems are caused by faulty cable connections (loose, unplugged, or mis-wired connectors); assume nothing, change only ONE thing at a time, and if it doesn't fix the fault, change it back before testing the next item. Option B. Cosmic radiation flipping DSP memory bits; change five settings at once to save time. Option C. Defective copper ore from the mine; replace all rack processors before checking power cords. Option D. Loudspeaker magnets losing magnetism overnight; never document what you changed.

clips.label: Question 291
clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Divide and Conquer (Half-Splitting) Fault Isolation Strategy. An auditorium audio chain (`Wireless Mic → Receiver → Mixer → DSP → Crossover → Power Amp → Loudspeaker`) has no output. To isolate the fault in the fewest steps using 'Divide and Conquer' (Half-Splitting), where should the technician test first? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Unsolder the voice coil inside the ceiling loudspeaker first. Option B. Split the signal chain near the accessible midpoint (e.g., checking meters or injecting/monitoring signal at the Mixer/DSP interface) to immediately eliminate half of the system, then bisect the failing half. Option C. Replace every piece of equipment from left to right starting with the microphone capsule. Option D. Rewrite the touch-panel GUI graphics.

clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Midpoint Cross-Plugging (Channel Swapping) Diagnostic Interpretation. Channel 1 of a stereo system is dead while Channel 2 works normally. At the midpoint between the mixer output and power amplifier input, you cross-plug Mixer Out 1 into Amp In 2, and Mixer Out 2 into Amp In 1. Now Speaker 1 plays normally and Speaker 2 is dead. Where is the fault? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Downstream in Power Amplifier Channel 1 or Loudspeaker 1. Option B. In the AC mains circuit breaker feeding the rack. Option C. Upstream in Mixer Channel 1 (because the fault moved from Output 1 to Output 2 when the upstream feeds were swapped at the midpoint). Option D. In the room's acoustic reverberation time.

A Blu-ray player works perfectly when plugged directly into Display 1, Display 2, or Display 3 individually, but all three displays go blank or show snow when fed simultaneously through a low-cost 1×4 HDMI Distribution Amplifier (DA). What is the root cause? Choose one labeled answer area. Option A. The inexpensive HDMI DA fails to manage HDCP repeater authentication and exhausts the source device's limited HDCP key count across multiple sinks; replace it with an HDCP-compliant repeater/DA with EDID/HDCP management. Option B. Blu-ray players can only output analog composite video. Option C. The displays need their contrast ratios reduced below 7:1. Option D. The room's ambient noise exceeds 35 dBA.

clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Systematic RS-232 Serial Control Fault Isolation Before Calling Programmer. A rack processor's RS-232 port stops controlling a display after a technician re-dressed the rear rack cables. What four hardware/configuration checks must the technician verify BEFORE calling the control programmer? Choose the best destination for the match. Option A. clips.label: Question 296
clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Diagnosing Non-Minimum Phase Acoustic Cancellation (Single vs. Multiple Locations). While troubleshooting a frequency-response dip in an auditorium, adjusting the DSP parametric equalizer produces zero acoustic change on the analyzer. How do you determine whether the root cause is a loudspeaker crossover/driver fault versus a room reflection? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Turn the equalizer boost up to +24 dB until the woofer smokes. Option B. Check the IP address of the equalizer. Option C. Measure at multiple locations: if the non-minimum-phase anomaly appears at MULTIPLE locations, it is a loudspeaker driver/crossover alignment issue; if it appears at ONE location only, it is a local room reflection. Option D. Replace the omnidirectional measurement mic with a piezo tweeter.

clips.label: Question 297
clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Tracing Unlabeled Copper Cables with an Inductive Tone Generator and Probe. During a repair visit to an older facility that lacks as-built drawings or cable labels, how should the technician identify which twisted-pair cable in a rack bundle runs to a specific wall plate? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Connect 120 V AC mains power to the wall plate and see which rack cable sparks. Option B. Cut every cable in the rack bundle one by one until the room goes dead. Option C. Use an Optical Time-Domain Reflectometer (OTDR) on the copper wire. Option D. Disconnect the cable from active electronics, attach an audio/RF tone generator ('fox') to the pair at the wall plate, and trace the signal inductively at the rack using a handheld inductive amplifier probe ('hound').

Sweeping the disconnected line with a `Z`-meter shows near-zero impedance. What mistake did the handyman likely make? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Option D. He used a fiberglass ladder instead of an aluminum ladder.

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Reporting Unpowered Copper Continuity Verification Before Energizing. Why must continuity and short-circuit testing of field-terminated copper audio, control, and data cables be completed and logged with all equipment UNPOWERED? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Because multimeters cannot measure voltage when equipment is turned on. Option B. Because live power makes the cable jacket shrink. Option C. Because continuity testers only work in complete darkness. Option D. Because injecting a multimeter's resistance test current into an energized circuit can damage the meter or equipment, and finding a short circuit before applying power prevents blowing fuses, PoE ports, or amplifier outputs.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Audio Gain Structure: Unity Gain (1 kHz DMM) vs. System Optimization (Pink Noise + Clipping). During audio commissioning, what is the critical difference between the **Unity Gain** method and the **System Optimization** method of setting gain structure—especially regarding power amplifiers? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Unity Gain connects power amplifiers first; System Optimization uses a 1 kHz sine wave into connected horns at full volume. Option B. Unity Gain uses a `1 kHz sine wave` and a DMM to set every electronic stage to `1:1 (0 dB)` voltage gain with power amplifiers **DISCONNECTED**; System Optimization uses broadband `pink noise` (and a 400 Hz piezo clip detector) to set each stage just below clipping for maximum dynamic range and SNR, then sets amplifier attenuators for target room SPL. Option C. Both methods require setting every input trim to maximum (+60 dB) and turning the master fader down to -40 dB. Option D. Unity Gain only works on HDMI audio, while System Optimization only works on cassette decks.

clips.label: Final Cram question 56
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Never Boost Deep Narrow Acoustic Cancellation Nulls with EQ. While viewing a room's acoustic measurement on an analyzer, the technician sees a sharp, narrow 15 dB dip (notch) at 250 Hz caused by a floor-bounce acoustic phase cancellation. Why must the technician **NEVER** apply +15 dB of parametric EQ boost at 250 Hz to flatten that dip? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Because DSP equalizers cannot adjust frequencies below 1 kHz. Option B. Because boosting 250 Hz turns off phantom power. Option C. Because 250 Hz is outside the human hearing range. Option D. Because an acoustic cancellation null affects both the direct wave and the out-of-phase reflected wave equally—so boosting 250 Hz by +15 dB eats up nearly 32x amplifier power and speaker excursion headroom without filling the null at that seat while booming loudly elsewhere in the room.

clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Firmware Update Discipline: Backup Config First and Read Release Notes. During a preventive maintenance visit, a technician considers updating the firmware on a room's DSP, control processor, and network switch. What mandatory discipline applies BEFORE loading any firmware update onto a working production AV system? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Update all devices simultaneously over public Wi-Fi five minutes before the CEO's global town hall. Option B. Factory-reset the DSP without saving a copy of the room file. Option C. First save and verify a full backup of the running configuration/code, read the manufacturer's firmware Release Notes to confirm compatibility and whether a specific security bug or feature actually warrants the update, and perform the update only during an approved maintenance window. Option D. Unplug the rack PDU halfway through the flash write cycle.

clips.label: Final Cram question 72
clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Handling Projector Lamps (Hg Vapor / Skin Oils) and Optical Engine Air Filters. When replacing an arc/UHP projector lamp module or cleaning projector/rack air intake filters during preventive maintenance, why must the technician NEVER touch the quartz glass bulb with bare fingers or blow compressed air inward through a dirty filter into the optical engine? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Because skin oils change the projector's IP address. Option B. Because quartz glass dissolves in water. Option C. Because dirty filters increase projector lumen output. Option D. Because skin oils create a localized thermal hot spot on the quartz envelope that causes the high-pressure mercury-vapor lamp to blister and shatter (and blowing dust inward contaminates internal LCD/DLP optics/polarizers); always let the lamp cool, wear gloves/eye protection, and vacuum/wash filters away from the intake.

clips.label: Final Cram question 75
clips.text: Exam area F. Topic: Ground-Loop Hum Diagnosis and Proper Technical Grounding vs. Lifting Safety Grounds. After replacing a podium audio interface connected to a main rack mixer plugged into a different branch circuit, a loud `60 Hz` (or `50 Hz`) buzz/hum appears in the room speakers whenever the podium interface is plugged into AC power. What is the root cause, and why is clipping off the AC plug's third-prong safety ground (`U-ground`) strictly forbidden? Choose the single best answer. Option A. The speaker wire is too thick; clipping the AC safety ground fixes speaker impedance. Option B. A ground loop caused by a voltage potential difference between two separate AC ground points is driving 50/60 Hz circulating current down the audio cable shield; lifting the AC safety ground pin is a lethal electrocution hazard and code violation—instead, bond both racks to the same technical ground point or insert an audio isolation transformer / optical isolator in the audio path. Option C. The room has too much acoustic absorption on the walls. Option D. The microphone needs +48 V phantom power turned on.
